ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows two nearby solenoids. The left solenoid is connected in a circuit with a battery and a variable resistor labeled R_Left. The battery’s longer plate is on the side connected through the resistor to the left lower terminal of the left solenoid, so conventional current initially enters the left solenoid at its left lower terminal and proceeds through the winding toward the right. The right solenoid is close to it and is wound in the same visible sense. Its circuit includes a resistor labeled R_right and an ammeter at the bottom. Reasoning: Increasing R_Left slowly decreases the current in the left-hand circuit. Therefore the magnetic flux produced by the left solenoid through the nearby right solenoid decreases. By Lenz’s law, the induced current in the right-hand circuit must oppose the decrease, so it must produce a magnetic field in the same direction as the original field from the left solenoid. Since the right solenoid is wound in the same sense, the required induced conventional current enters the right solenoid at its left lower terminal, leaves at the right lower terminal, then goes down through R_right and through the ammeter from right to left. Thus the ammeter needle deflects to the left.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the left solenoid is connected to a battery and variable resistor R_Left; the long battery plate is on the resistor/left-terminal side, so conventional current initially enters the left lower terminal of the left solenoid and goes through the winding toward the right. The right solenoid is close to it, wound in the same visible sense, and its lower circuit contains R_right and an ammeter. Use the right-hand grip rule on the drawn winding to find the magnetic field produced by the left solenoid through the nearby right solenoid. Since the text says R_Left is slowly increased, the primary current and therefore this flux decrease. By Lenz's law, the induced current in the right solenoid must create magnetic field in the same direction as the decreasing original flux. Applying the right-hand grip rule to the right solenoid with the same winding sense shows the induced current must enter the right solenoid at its left lower terminal, leave at the right terminal, go down through R_right, and pass through the ammeter from right to left. Therefore the ammeter needle deflects to the left.

method.method_draft: Use a transformer/dot-convention sign method. From the image, note that the two solenoids have the same handedness and are magnetically coupled. Assign corresponding dotted terminals to the lower-left terminal of each solenoid: current entering such a terminal would produce the same axial flux direction in both coils. The battery polarity in the left circuit shows the primary current enters the dotted terminal of the left solenoid. The text change, increasing R_Left, means this dotted-terminal primary current is decreasing, so di_p/dt is negative. With the mutual-inductance convention v_s(dot minus undot) = M di_p/dt, the dotted terminal of the right solenoid becomes at lower potential than its undotted terminal. Thus the secondary current in the external right-hand circuit flows from the undotted/right coil terminal through R_right and then through the ammeter toward the dotted/left coil terminal, i.e. through the ammeter from right to left. That corresponds to a left deflection of the needle.

图像描述：图中有两个相互靠近的螺线管。左边螺线管接在含有可变电阻 R_left 和电池的闭合回路中；电池的长极板在左侧，表示左侧为正极。右边螺线管接在含有 R_right 和电流表的闭合回路中。两个螺线管绕线方向相同，因此可用相同的点标记约定来判断互感极性：把两个线圈的下左端视为对应的 dotted terminal。

推理：按图中电池极性，左边原边电流从电池正极经 R_left 进入左螺线管的下左端，也就是进入 dotted terminal。题目说左侧电阻 R_left 被慢慢增大，因此原边电流减小，即 di_p/dt < 0。按互感点约定，右侧线圈满足 v_s(dot minus undot) = M di_p/dt。由于 di_p/dt 为负，右侧 dotted terminal，即右螺线管下左端，电势低于 undotted terminal，即下右端。于是右侧回路中的感应常规电流从右线圈下右端流出，经过 R_right，再经过电流表流向右线圈下左端；也就是通过电流表时方向为从右向左。题目说明电流表指针表示常规电流方向，因此指针向左偏转。
